fetch.because: Article 3 grants the right to reproduce and transmit the product, which is what paging the service performs, and article 6 states that access and provision are free.

extract.because: Article 3 grants adaptation (`aanpassen`) alongside reproduction, which covers reading the designator and the component references out of a feature. transform.because: Article 3 grants re-use for any lawful purpose including adaptation and commercial exploitation, so joining the four feature types into a token and tag corpus is granted. Article 4 adds one obligation that carries into the result: attribution as `Bron: Digitaal Vlaanderen`.

train.because: Article 3's `elk rechtmatig doeleinde` reserves no act of analysis, and article 5 states that the licensee holds the intellectual property in the works it creates on the basis of the product. Article 4 requires that the re-use not breach data-protection law, which this source's `personalDataReview` addresses.

redistribute-data.because: Article 3 grants publication and transmission. Article 4 conditions it on the attribution the licensor specified, `Bron: Digitaal Vlaanderen`, and provides the wording for a combined work where listing every source is impractical: `bevat overheidsinformatie, verkregen onder de modellicentie voor gratis hergebruik Vlaanderen v1.0`. redistribute-model.because: This instrument answers the question CC BY leaves open. Article 5 states that the licensee retains all intellectual property rights in the works it creates on the basis of the product, `zonder evenwel afbreuk te doen aan de verplichtingen betreffende het hergebruik van het product in deze werken`. Trained weights are such a work, so they are the licensee's, and the product's attribution obligation carries into them.

commercial-sublicense.because: Article 3 grants a non-exclusive right to the licensee and states no sublicensing right, and article 5 reserves to the licensor every right the licence does not grant. Unlike CC BY 4.0 §2(a)(5)(A), this instrument makes no direct offer to a downstream recipient, so whether a recipient holds it by taking the product under the same standing public licence is a question the text does not answer. sources.authorityBasis: Cadastral authority for Spain; publishes the INSPIRE Addresses (AD) theme as an ATOM download service under its own access-and-use licence

sources.note: The AD theme is an address point at a building entrance carrying a house-number designator; a thoroughfare name; a postcode and a municipality. It carries no party.
sources.coverage: The INSPIRE Addresses (AD) theme of the Dirección General del Catastro, reached through the ATOM download service at `https://www.catastro.hacienda.gob.es/INSPIRE/Addresses/ES.SDGC.AD.atom.xml`, 681,783 bytes, sha256 `4342d37b6d5527eb7b8bebadc97966c90f1a041068ae9398b90183f2176898b9`, carrying `<updated>2026-08-21T00:00:00Z</updated>`. The feed lists 55 entries, and this row covers 52 of them. The other three belong to the Provincial Councils of Bizkaia, Gipuzkoa and Navarra, which publish their own cadastres through the same feed and state their own terms, `CC BY 3.0 ES`, `CC-BY-SA` and `CC BY 4.0`. Adding them needs a row each, because a decision scoped to one publisher cannot reach another. Each of the 52 entries links a province feed listing one zipped GML per municipality. The measured instance is Ceuta, `A.ES.SDGC.AD.55101.zip`, 354,647 bytes, whose one member `A.ES.SDGC.AD.55101.gml` is 11,861,975 bytes and holds 8,126 `AD:Address` features. A feature is a point at a building entrance carrying a house-number designator, and it references a thoroughfare name, a postal descriptor and an administrative unit by `xlink:href`. The row count for the other 51 offices was not measured.

personalDataReview.because: Every element name in `A.ES.SDGC.AD.55101.gml` was counted over all 11,861,975 bytes, so this covers the file rather than its first features. It holds 48 distinct element names and none of them names a party: there is no owner, holder, `titular`, occupant or contact element, and no personal name of any kind. The only names are 505 `AD:ThoroughfareName`, 5 `AD:PostalDescriptor` and 1 `AD:AdminUnitName`. The file declares the INSPIRE Addresses 3.0 schema at `urn:x-inspire:specification:gmlas:Addresses:3.0`, which has no party element for another municipality to populate, so the reading rests on the schema as well as on the one municipality read. This is what separates the row from the other 25 `verified-corpus` sources: each of those is a business register or a procurement portal where the address belongs to a party, and some of those parties are natural persons trading on their own account. The cadastre's AD theme records the place. The ownership data that Spanish cadastral records also hold travels through a separate protected channel and appears nowhere in this dataset.

sources.coverage: The INSPIRE Addresses (AD) theme of Kadaster, reached through the ATOM download service at `https://service.pdok.nl/kadaster/ad/atom/adressen_inspire_geharmoniseerd.xml`, 2,247 bytes, sha256 `36c587f04c6c4e57c71fd03ff253d85df3c8d796b9c12c26159dda1e0262effe`. The feed holds one entry covering the whole country rather than one per municipality, so this row's coverage is national and measured rather than inferred from a sample. That entry is `https://service.pdok.nl/kadaster/ad/atom/downloads/addresses.gml.gz`, 819,465,603 bytes, sha256 `7ea1e45ee200327468eab8c8089a46ad99c334606cae19df7ba334cfae34cd5f`, which expands to 29,677,448,685 bytes of GML holding **10,066,060 address features**. That is the largest measured address count of any source in this register.

personalDataReview.because: Every element name in the decompressed GML was counted over all 29,677,448,685 bytes, read as a stream, so this covers the whole country rather than a sample of it. The file holds 49 distinct element names across 10,066,060 address features, and none of them identifies a party: there is no owner, holder, occupant or contact element, and no personal name. The four names outside the address, geographical-name and geometry vocabulary are `identifier`, `nameParts`, `PartOfName` and `part`, and the last three are the INSPIRE structure that splits a thoroughfare name into its components. The file follows the INSPIRE Addresses schema, which has no party element.

sources.coverage: The INSPIRE Addresses (AD) theme of the Czech Office for Surveying, Mapping and Cadastre, reached through the ATOM download service at `https://atom.cuzk.gov.cz/AD/AD.xml`, 8,373,817 bytes, sha256 `9b1d51a721ab601fa74307cce5ce20f74d12dd29512f87be29cd1072f0a2d83b`. personalDataReview.because: Every element name in `584061.xml` was counted over all 1,164,835 bytes, so this covers the file rather than its first features. It holds 53 distinct element names across 304 address features, and none of them identifies a party: there is no owner, holder, occupant or contact element, and no personal name. sources.name: DK INSPIRE Addresses
sources.authorityBasis: National geodata agency for Denmark; publishes the INSPIRE Addresses (AD) theme as an ATOM download service serving a GeoPackage for the whole country
sources.access: ATOM download service; one zipped GeoPackage for the whole country
sources.note: The address table carries a house-number designator and references a thoroughfare name and a postal descriptor. It carries no party column.
sources.coverage: The INSPIRE Addresses (AD) theme of Klimadatastyrelsen, reached through the ATOM download service at `https://www2.sdfe.dk/INSPIRE/feeds/Addresses.xml`, 3,130 bytes, sha256 `5a32be44b186586dbef5efa24bd200b3d2d85afebb74172250f5dd977d3ddbea`. Denmark serves this theme as a GeoPackage rather than as GML, which is why `addressRoles` is keyed by a table name instead of an element name. The feed holds one entry covering the whole country. Its dataset is `DK_INSPIRE_Addresses.zip`, 101,406,038 bytes, sha256 `0b4e13e27307659ac64065e8f67301b4eb649faa35e6e29f8f443f51c91c5141`, whose member `ad_inspire.gpkg` is 391,258,112 bytes. The database declares five tables in `gpkg_contents`: `address` with 599,999 rows, `thoroughfarename` with 112,488, `addressareaname` with 7,840, `postaldescriptor` with 1,089 and `adminunitname` with 105. **Treat 599,999 as a possible export cap rather than as Denmark's address count**: it is one short of a round 600,000, and the national address register holds several times that. Establishing the true extent means asking the publisher or finding a second distribution. Two reader notes. The feed writes its one entry as `<entry xml:lang="da">`, so a reader matching a bare `<entry>` finds none. And the Atom entry's href returns the weblink's listing page; the file needs `&realfilename=DK_INSPIRE_Addresses.zip` appended.

personalDataReview.because: Every column of every table the GeoPackage declares was listed, so this covers the database's whole schema rather than a sample of its rows. The five tables carry 39, 16, 15, 15 and 15 columns, and none of the 100 identifies a party: there is no owner, holder, occupant or contact column, and no personal name. Every column of the `address` table is INSPIRE address structure, being an identifier, a lifespan date, a position, a locator designator, or a reference to a thoroughfare name, postal descriptor, administrative unit, parcel or building. One value invites a misreading: `position_method` reads `byotherparty`, which is an INSPIRE codelist term for how the position was determined rather than a reference to a party. The schema is the INSPIRE Addresses model, which has no party element.

sources.name: EE INSPIRE Addresses (AD)
sources.authorityBasis: National land and space agency for Estonia; publishes the INSPIRE Addresses (AD) theme as a direct-access Web Feature Service covering the whole country
sources.access: WFS 2.0 download service; paged GetFeature in GeoJSON or GML
sources.note: A feature is an address point with an address identifier designator and a site or building name. It carries no party.
sources.coverage: The INSPIRE Addresses (AD) theme of Maa- ja Ruumiamet, reached as a WFS 2.0 download service at `https://inspire.geoportaal.ee/geoserver/AD_Address/wfs`. The service publishes all five AD feature types and advertises `ImplementsResultPaging`, so a build pages each type rather than downloading a file. Measured 2026-09-30, `resultType=hits` past index 0 reports 729,973 `AD.Address` features, and a page of the type agreed with that count. The component types report 19,676 `AD.Address_ThoroughfareName`, 4,800 `AD.Address_AdminUnitName`, 638 `AD.Address_AddressAreaName` and 1,374,116 `AD.Address_PostalDescriptor`, the last of which exceeds the address count and therefore carries more than one descriptor per address. Two reader notes. This service names its types under its own prefix, `AD_Address:AD.Address` and `AD_Address:AD.Address_ThoroughfareName`, so a reader comparing the part after the colon against `Address` finds no address type here. And it advertises `application/geo+json` and answers a `GetFeature` for it with `InvalidParameterValue: Failed to find response for output format`, while the same request under `application/json` returns the features.

personalDataReview.because: Every property of all five feature types was listed, over 40 features each: 37 on `AD.Address`, 20 on `AD.Address_AdminUnitName`, 15 on `AD.Address_ThoroughfareName`, 15 on `AD.Address_AddressAreaName` and 14 on `AD.Address_PostalDescriptor`. None of the 101 identifies a party, and each is INSPIRE address structure, being an identifier, a lifespan date, a status, a position, a locator, a name or a component reference. `AD:LocatorName` needs its own statement because it is free text of type `GeographicalName`, which is how a family name or a business name reaches an INSPIRE address, and this publisher populates it where the Dutch, Czech and Danish themes leave it empty: 1,200 of 1,200 addresses sampled over 60 windows spread across the 729,973, reaching 664 distinct locality paths, carry a value. Every one of those 1,200 states its `LocatorNameTypeValue` as `siteName` (829) or `buildingName` (371), which are place designations in the INSPIRE codelist, and no value takes the given-name-and-family-name shape: 0 of 1,200 carry two capitalized words, while 105 carry a hyphen. The values are Estonian farm and site names, which is how a rural Estonian address designates its addressable unit, as in `Saare maakond, Muhu vald, Raugi küla, Jüri`. Some are the genitive of a personal given name, `Jüri`, `Jaani`, `Mardi` and `Hansi` among them, which is the traditional pattern of naming a farm after a historical householder rather than a reference to the present occupant, and the compounds confirm it: `Vana-Käspri` and `Uue-Tooma` read as the old and the new holding of a named farm. No element asserts a party, states a surname, or carries a person identifier.

sources.name: Flanders INSPIRE Adressen (AD)
sources.authorityBasis: Digital agency of the Flemish government and manager of the Flemish spatial data infrastructure; publishes the INSPIRE Addresses (AD) theme for the Flemish Region as a direct-access Web Feature Service
sources.access: WFS 2.0 download service; paged GetFeature in GeoJSON or GML
sources.note: A feature is an address point with a house-number designator that references a street name and a postal descriptor. It carries no party. Coverage is the Flemish Region rather than Belgium.
sources.coverage: The INSPIRE Addresses (AD) theme of agentschap Digitaal Vlaanderen, reached as a WFS 2.0 download service at `https://geo.api.vlaanderen.be/ad/wfs`. **Coverage is the Flemish Region rather than Belgium**: Brussels and Wallonia publish the theme through their own services, so this row is one of three a Belgian build needs. Measured 2026-09-30, `resultType=hits` past index 0 reports 4,563,062 `ad:Address` features, and a page of the type agreed with that count. A bare hits request without a `startIndex` reports 10000 instead, which is a per-request cap rather than a count, so this service must be asked past index 0. It publishes four of the five AD feature types, omitting `ad:AddressAreaName`, and the component types report their own counts separately. An address references its components by the identifier URI its component features publish in `identifier`, such as `https://data.vlaanderen.be/id/straatnaam/6301`, which joins locally. On a page of five addresses, 5 of the 20 references instead address `http://vocab.belgif.be/auth/refnis1995/1000#id`, a term in the Belgian NIS vocabulary, so those administrative-unit components live outside this service and an address carrying one is complete at its source rather than incomplete here.

personalDataReview.because: Every property of all four feature types was listed, over 40 features each: 9 on `ad:Address`, 8 on `ad:AdminUnitName`, 8 on `ad:PostalDescriptor` and 7 on `ad:ThoroughfareName`. None of the 32 identifies a party, and each is INSPIRE address structure, being an identifier, a lifespan date, a status, a validity date, a position, a locator, a name, a postcode or a component reference. `AD:LocatorName` is the element that needs its own statement, because it is free text of type `GeographicalName` and the one way a family name or a business name reaches an INSPIRE address. This service leaves it empty: 0 of 800 addresses sampled over 40 windows spread across the 4,563,062 populate it, and the `locator` carries only a `designator` and a `level`. The designator values are house numbers typed `LocatorDesignatorTypeValue/addressIdentifierGeneral`. Article 4 of the elected licence requires that a re-use not breach data-protection law, and this reading is the measurement behind that undertaking for this source.
